**Date:** 2026-01-12

## Current Toolkit Misalignments

Based on analysis of the CORTEX codebase, here are actual toolkit issues that would be identified by the enhanced brittleness review prompt (v2.1.0):

---

## 🔴 Critical Issues (Phase 2)

### AC-TOOLKIT-001: Consolidate Audit Tool Family
```yaml
id: AC-TOOLKIT-001
title: "Consolidate audit tool family"
description: |
  Multiple audit-related tools exist with overlapping functionality:
  - audit_based_evidence_validator.py (scripts/)
  - audit_log_manager.py (scripts/)
  - query_audit_trail.py (scripts/)
  - verify_audit_trail.py (scripts/)
  
  These should be consolidated into src/mcp/audit-tools.py with
  multiple @mcp_tool decorated functions, each with full docstring
  and metadata. Move from scripts/ to core toolkit.
  
  Desired state: Single audit-tools.py module in src/mcp/ with:
  - @mcp_tool: audit_query(db_path, filters)
  - @mcp_tool: audit_validate(evidence_path)
  - @mcp_tool: audit_history(ac_id, days)
  - Internal: _parse_filters(), _validate_entries()

category: consolidation
priority: critical
phase: 2
type: consolidation
effort: medium
estimated_hours: 8

current_state: |
  4 separate Python files in scripts/ directory with
  overlapping functionality, no @mcp_tool decorators,
  no unified error handling, scattered across file system

desired_state: |
  Single audit-tools.py in src/mcp/ with:
  - All unique capabilities merged
  - @mcp_tool decorators on public functions
  - Consistent error handling (status/data/error format)
  - Complete test coverage in tests/mcp/test-audit-tools.py
  - Registered in capability_registry.py discovery

impact: |
  - MasterOrchestrator will have single audit interface
  - Cleaner imports (one module vs four)
  - Better test coverage
  - Reduced code duplication
  - Improved discoverability (single module name)

implementation: |
  1. Create src/mcp/audit-tools.py
  2. Merge unique functions from 4 audit scripts
  3. Add @mcp_tool decorators with metadata
  4. Implement consistent error handling
  5. Write comprehensive tests in tests/mcp/test-audit-tools.py
  6. Update imports in all dependent code
  7. Delete original audit scripts (or archive)
  8. Verify capability_registry discovers new tools

verification: |
  1. Run pytest tests/mcp/test-audit-tools.py (100% pass)
  2. Verify capability_registry.get("cortex_audit_query") returns tool
  3. Check no circular imports
  4. Validate CORE-024 compliance (@mcp_tool metadata complete)
  5. Ensure no functionality lost in consolidation

tests:
  - tests/mcp/test-audit-tools.py
dependencies:
  - []
evidence_paths:
  - scripts/audit_based_evidence_validator.py
  - scripts/audit_log_manager.py
  - scripts/query_audit_trail.py
  - scripts/verify_audit_trail.py
status: planned
ac_standard: AC-TOOLKIT-001
```

### AC-TOOLKIT-002: Rename Tools to Remove Adjectives & Enforce Kebab-Case

```yaml
id: AC-TOOLKIT-002
title: "Rename tools: Remove adjectives, enforce kebab-case (CORE-022)"
description: |
  Multiple tools violate CORE-022 naming standards:
  - "new-audit-query.py" → REMOVE adjective "new"
  - "enhanced-evidence-generator.py" → REMOVE adjective "enhanced"
  - "updated-state-manager.py" → REMOVE adjective "updated"
  - "legacy-orchestrator.py" → REMOVE adjective "legacy"
  - "real_implementation_engine.py" → CONVERT to kebab-case
  - "ultimate_evidence_validator.py" → CONVERT to kebab-case
  - "duplicate-detection-toolkit.py" → REDUCE to 25 chars (currently 36)
  
  Complies with CORE-022: File naming must be kebab-case, ≤25 chars,
  no adjectives (new/old/updated/enhanced/legacy/temp/etc).

category: naming
priority: high
phase: 2
type: naming
effort: low
estimated_hours: 4

violations_found:
  - file: new-audit-query.py
    violations: ["adjective-'new'"]
    remediation: "Rename to audit-query.py"
    
  - file: enhanced-evidence-generator.py
    violations: ["adjective-'enhanced'", "length-26-chars"]
    remediation: "Rename to evidence-generator.py"
    
  - file: real_implementation_engine.py
    violations: ["snake-case", "length-26-chars"]
    remediation: "Rename to implementation-engine.py"
    
  - file: ultimate_evidence_validator.py
    violations: ["snake-case", "length-27-chars", "adjective-'ultimate'"]
    remediation: "Rename to evidence-validator.py"
    
  - file: duplicate-detection-toolkit.py
    violations: ["length-36-chars (max-25)", "adjective-'toolkit'"]
    remediation: "Rename to duplicate-detector.py"

current_state: |
  Tools scattered across scripts/ and src/tools/ with
  inconsistent naming. Adjectives like "new", "enhanced",
  "updated", "legacy" violate CORE-022. Snake_case used
  instead of kebab-case. Multiple files exceed 25 chars.

desired_state: |
  All tools follow CORE-022 standard:
  - kebab-case (hyphens, lowercase)
  - ≤25 characters (excluding .py)
  - NO adjectives
  - Capability-focused names
  
  Examples:
  - audit-query.py ✅
  - evidence-generator.py ✅
  - implementation-engine.py ✅
  - evidence-validator.py ✅
  - duplicate-detector.py ✅

implementation: |
  1. For each violating file:
     a. Determine correct name (remove adjectives, convert case, shorten)
     b. Rename file (git mv old_name new_name)
     c. Update all imports across codebase
     d. Update @mcp_tool name parameter if applicable
     e. Update capability_registry references
     f. Verify tests still pass
  2. Run find command to verify no violations remain
  3. Update TOOLKIT-DESIGN-REFERENCE.md examples if needed

verification: |
  1. Run: find src/ -name "*.py" -type f | xargs -I {} basename {} | \
          grep -E '[A-Z]|_|new|old|enhanced|updated|legacy|temp'
     Should return: empty (no violations)
  2. Verify all files in kebab-case: ✅
  3. Verify all files ≤25 chars: ✅
  4. Verify no adjectives: ✅
  5. Run tests: 100% pass with new names
  6. Verify capability_registry discovers tools with new names

tests:
  - Existing tests (should pass after import updates)
  - No new tests required (naming-only change)
dependencies:
  - []
evidence_paths:
  - src/tools/
  - scripts/
status: planned
ac_standard: AC-TOOLKIT-002
```

### AC-TOOLKIT-003: Add @mcp_tool Decorators (CORE-024 Enforcement)

```yaml
id: AC-TOOLKIT-003
title: "Expose all public tools via @mcp_tool decorator (CORE-024)"
description: |
  CORE-024 requires: "Enforce @mcp_tool decorator for all MCP tools - prevent registration drift"
  
  Currently, several public-facing tools are NOT decorated:
  - evidence_bundle_generator.py (should be @mcp_tool)
  - traceability_matrix_generator.py (should be @mcp_tool)
  - gap_detector.py (should be @mcp_tool)
  - validate-prompt-integrity.py (should be @mcp_tool)
  - consolidate-documents.py (should be @mcp_tool)
  - reorganize-cx6-docs.py (should be @mcp_tool)
  
  These tools are executable but invisible to MasterOrchestrator's
  capability registry, creating registration blind spots.
  
  Remediation: Add @mcp_tool decorator to each public tool function.

category: mcp-exposure
priority: critical
phase: 2
type: exposure
effort: medium
estimated_hours: 6

discovery_status: "8 tools missing @mcp_tool decorator"
risk: "MasterOrchestrator cannot discover these tools"

tools_requiring_decoration:
  - evidence_bundle_generator.py
  - traceability_matrix_generator.py
  - gap_detector.py
  - validate_prompt_integrity.py
  - consolidate_documents.py
  - reorganize_cx6_docs.py
  - (and 2 more from initial audit)

decorator_template: |
  @mcp_tool(
      name="cortex_<tool_name>",
      description="<clear description of what tool does>",
      category="<category: audit|governance|planning|development|maintenance>",
      parameters={
          "<param_name>": {
              "type": "<type>",
              "required": True|False,
              "description": "<description>"
          },
          ...
      },
      returns={
          "type": "object",
          "description": "Result with status, data, error keys"
      },
      metadata={
          "tags": ["<tag1>", "<tag2>"],
          "version": "1.0",
          "autonomous": True|False,
          "ac_standard": "AC-TOOLKIT-003"
      }
  )

current_state: |
  Tools exist and are functional but NOT exposed to MCP system.
  capability_registry._discover_decorated_tools() cannot find them.
  MasterOrchestrator has no way to call these tools programmatically.

desired_state: |
  All public tools have @mcp_tool decorator with:
  - Proper metadata (name, description, category)
  - Parameter definitions (type, required, description)
  - Returns definition (consistent format)
  - Metadata tags (for discoverability)
  
  Each tool discoverable via:
  registry = get_capability_registry()
  tool = registry.get("cortex_<tool_name>")

implementation: |
  For each undecorate tool:
  1. Identify public entry point function
  2. Add @mcp_tool decorator with complete metadata
  3. Update imports (add: from src.mcp.mcp_decorator import mcp_tool)
  4. Ensure function has clear docstring
  5. Add tool module to capability_registry._discover_decorated_tools()
     import list if not already there
  6. Verify tool is discovered after import
  7. Write test: test_tool_in_capability_registry()
  
  Example addition to capability_registry.py:
    'src.mcp.traceability_tools',  # NEW

verification: |
  1. Import each decorated tool module
  2. Verify decorator registers tool:
     from src.mcp.mcp_decorator import get_decorated_tools
     tools = get_decorated_tools()
     assert any(t['name'] == 'cortex_evidence_generator' for t in tools)
  3. Verify capability_registry discovers tool:
     registry = get_capability_registry()
     tool = registry.get("cortex_evidence_generator")
     assert tool is not None
  4. Check metadata is complete:
     assert tool.metadata['tags']
     assert tool.metadata['version']
     assert tool.metadata['ac_standard']
  5. Run pytest tests/mcp/test_<tool>_tools.py

tests:
  - tests/mcp/test_<tool>_tools.py (each tool)
  - tests/mcp/test_capability_registry.py (discovery test)
dependencies:
  - AC-TOOLKIT-002 (naming standardization)
evidence_paths:
  - src/tools/
  - src/mcp/
status: planned
ac_standard: AC-TOOLKIT-003
```

## 🟡 High-Priority Issues (Phase 3)

### AC-TOOLKIT-004: Move Operational Scripts to Toolkit

```yaml
id: AC-TOOLKIT-004
title: "Refactor operational scripts into CORTEX toolkit"
description: |
  Currently, many operational/utility scripts exist in scripts/
  that should be consolidated into the toolkit:
  
  Scripts to consolidate:
  - sync_plan_viewer_data.py → sync-plan-viewer.py (toolkit)
  - update_plan_viewer_progress.py → update-plan-viewer.py (toolkit)
  - validate_plan_viewer_links.py → validate-plan-links.py (toolkit)
  - generate_all_evidence_bundles.py → generate-evidence.py (toolkit)
  - consolidate_documents.py → consolidate-docs.py (toolkit)
  
  These should be:
  1. Moved to src/tools/ or src/mcp/
  2. Renamed per CORE-022 (kebab-case, ≤25 chars)
  3. Decorated with @mcp_tool
  4. Tested in tests/mcp/test_<tool>_tools.py

category: organization
priority: high
phase: 3
type: organization
effort: high
estimated_hours: 12

scripts_to_consolidate:
  - sync_plan_viewer_data.py
  - update_plan_viewer_progress.py
  - validate_plan_viewer_links.py
  - generate_all_evidence_bundles.py
  - consolidate_documents.py
  - reorganize_cx6_docs.py
  - (and 10+ more utility scripts)

benefits: |
  - Single toolkit source of truth (no scripts/ orphans)
  - All tools discoverable via MCP
  - Consistent naming and structure
  - Centralized testing
  - Better dependency management

implementation: |
  1. For each script:
     a. Determine primary function
     b. Rename per CORE-022 (kebab-case, ≤25 chars)
     c. Move to src/tools/ or src/mcp/
     d. Add @mcp_tool decorator (if public)
     e. Add import to capability_registry
     f. Update any imports across codebase
     g. Delete original script
     h. Write tests

verification: |
  1. All scripts/ directory is clean (only pre-commit hook, old files for archive)
  2. All operational tools are in src/tools/ or src/mcp/
  3. All tools have @mcp_tool or documented reason for exclusion
  4. capability_registry discovers all tools (100%)
  5. All tests pass (100%)

tests:
  - tests/mcp/test_sync_plan_viewer.py
  - tests/mcp/test_update_plan_viewer.py
  - tests/mcp/test_validate_plan_links.py
  - tests/mcp/test_evidence_generator.py
  - tests/mcp/test_consolidate_docs.py
dependencies:
  - AC-TOOLKIT-001 (consolidation)
  - AC-TOOLKIT-002 (naming)
  - AC-TOOLKIT-003 (MCP exposure)
evidence_paths:
  - scripts/ (directory to clean)
status: planned
ac_standard: AC-TOOLKIT-004
```

## 🟢 Medium-Priority Issues (Phase 3)

### AC-TOOLKIT-005: Create Toolkit Catalog & Documentation

```yaml
id: AC-TOOLKIT-005
title: "Create CORTEX toolkit catalog and discovery documentation"
description: |
  Create a human-readable toolkit catalog document that:
  - Lists all tools with descriptions
  - Shows tool categories and tags
  - Explains MCP exposure model
  - Provides examples of tool usage
  - Links to test files
  - Shows tool health metrics
  
  This document helps MasterOrchestrator operators understand
  what tools are available without diving into code.

category: documentation
priority: medium
phase: 3
type: documentation
effort: low
estimated_hours: 4

deliverable: |
  cortex-brain/documents/TOOLKIT-CATALOG.md
  
  Structure:
  - Overview (what is CORTEX toolkit)
  - Tool Categories (audit, governance, planning, etc.)
  - Tools by Category (name, description, examples)
  - Health Metrics (coverage, exposure, testing)
  - Tool Usage Examples
  - Troubleshooting Guide
  - Tool Development Guide

content_to_include: |
  For each tool:
  - Tool name (kebab-case)
  - Description (capability-focused)
  - Category and tags
  - Parameters (if public)
  - Example usage
  - Test coverage status
  - Related tools

implementation: |
  1. Generate from capability_registry:
     from src.mcp.capability_registry import get_capability_registry
     registry = get_capability_registry()
     tools = registry.list_all()
     for tool in tools:
         # Extract metadata and generate documentation
  2. Format as markdown with clear sections
  3. Add examples and usage patterns
  4. Include health metrics
  5. Add to cortex-brain/documents/

verification: |
  1. Document exists: cortex-brain/documents/TOOLKIT-CATALOG.md
  2. All public tools are listed
  3. Each tool has description and example
  4. Health metrics are accurate
  5. Links are valid (relative paths)

tests:
  - Verify markdown syntax is valid
  - Verify all tool names match actual tools
  - Verify no broken links
dependencies:
  - AC-TOOLKIT-001 through AC-TOOLKIT-004
evidence_paths:
  - cortex-brain/documents/TOOLKIT-CATALOG.md
status: planned
ac_standard: AC-TOOLKIT-005
```
